---
applyTo: "packages/web-platform/web-core-e2e/midscene/**"
---

Keep the CI screenshot table separate from the HTML report. Publish the report
index generated by Midscene Test's `mergeReportFiles`, and use its returned
`mergedReportPath` for links: embedded screenshots can produce a standalone
HTML file, while file-backed screenshots produce a directory with `index.html`.
Keep the vendored renderer byte-for-byte aligned with
`lynx/testing/ai_e2e/scripts/render-ci-summary.mjs`.

If Pages is unavailable, show the repository setup path in the job Summary and
skip publication without failing the test jobs. Gate the reusable publisher on
the publication artifact upload outcome, not just the preparation job result.

The upstream Pages site also hosts the production website. Route both website
and Midscene deployments through `workflow-pages.yml`, with reports reserved
under `/midscene/`. Hold the shared publisher concurrency lock across archive
restore, composition, persistence, and deployment. Preserve the other component
on every update. Never deploy a report-only artifact over the upstream website;
archive early reports until the first website build initializes the shared site.
Keep the upstream repository identity in the reusable workflow's
`MIDSCENE_UPSTREAM_REPOSITORY` environment variable. Both legacy archive import
and site composition use it; the CLI must reject missing identity configuration.
Resolve the public origin from Pages metadata, including custom domains. Keep
producer summaries limited to result counts and artifact downloads, without
case tables or empty screenshot columns, and add linked screenshots after deployment
succeeds. Default publication to the repository default branch without requiring
an Actions variable. Initial Pages enablement still needs a repository admin.

Use `aiAct` for visible user interactions instead of custom selector-based
action nodes. Preserve assertions required by the original upstream case;
do not replace exact event-payload or pixel comparisons with AI judgment.
Use aiWaitFor for readiness, without adding redundant validation contracts.
For one-click toggles, stop after the successful input even when its label
remains visible. Do not ask the planner to correct an already successful click
to the exact text center: a second click reverses the source state. Inspect
actual action counts and before/after screenshots when a deterministic
assertion fails. Use public deepThink planning with independent visual location
for the animation-event toggles; keep all original ordered assertions and
the four source interactions. A prompt-contract unit test is not model-backed
proof that the agent emits exactly one physical click.
The frame-data update action also uses independent deepThink grounding.
Compare the actual screenshot dimensions and physical tap with the model's
claimed dimensions before diagnosing a missed text action as a product defect.
Never add saved coordinates or repeat input to compensate for a wrong conversion.
Keep the two repeated blue-cell lazy-component cases in their original CSR
Playwright runner, with all three original browser profiles, both ordered inputs,
the 500/100/100 ms waits and all six source CSS checks. Do not count them as AI
replacements or change their fixtures. Independent grounding is insufficient for contiguous same-color
targets: the locator can return the whole column's center on an invisible
boundary, and a one-pixel difference can change which component receives input.
Preserve failed-attempt evidence and do not accept a correct retry as proof of
stable source-equivalent input. Keep original deterministic input contracts
unless a separately approved fixture change makes the targets distinguishable.
For requestAnimationFrame/cancelAnimationFrame text controls, use independent
visual grounding rather than inline coordinate arithmetic. Retain the original
1000/100/100 ms waits and ordered loop/stop text counts. Derive the contract from
the source callback and expectHasText helper, not a duplicate expected YAML.
Matching those waits does not establish click-relative timing equivalence.
Do not count a visual pilot as a complete source mapping. Bindtap and reload
contracts retain the original ordered inline-style reads with immediate checks
and original waits. The public LynxView reload API must not become a browser
refresh, and the reload page-count case does not replace the clicked-state case.
Keep keyboard input contracts in their original runner when key-down/key-up
separation, modifier payloads or an intentionally unfocused page are under test.
Do not focus a target or replace separated key phases with one AI keypress.
Run the six keyboard contracts in both CSR and SSR using the original three
browser profiles and bounded workers; do not count them as additional AI cases.
Likewise retain exact CDP touch trajectories, mouse down/up phases and wheel
deltas in the original pointer runner, including its CSR/SSR modes and original
browser guards. Ordinary textarea and scrollable-toggle clicks use aiAct.
An aiAct promise can settle seconds after the physical input because of
post-action planning. Matching a source wait in YAML therefore does not preserve
click-relative sampling. Retain `api-animate` in its original CSR runner
with all three browser profiles, both original PNGs and unchanged matcher
options. Its AI case is supplementary end-state evidence, not a replacement
for the original timing-sensitive contract. Inspect actual action timestamps
before claiming equivalence; do not compensate with a guessed shorter wait.
Follow the enabled upstream render matrix, currently CSR only, for this PNG
contract. The SSR shell omits the CSR margin reset, shifting the original image
by 8 px before input. Do not claim SSR pixel parity or change a baseline merely
because the source helper can navigate to an SSR URL.
Pixel tolerances belong to exact source PNG paths: preserve original exceptions
without applying them to neighboring snapshots or the web-elements suite.
Give every retained Playwright invocation a distinct output directory. The
runner clears its configured output before execution, so a later suite must
not erase an earlier suite's failure traces before the final artifact upload.
When migrating a new case, map every original assertion target, repeated-selector
index, value, comparison, and interaction sequence. Keep exact CSS and bounding-box
checks deterministic; do not round measurements or replace pixel contracts with
AI judgment. Create visual report evidence before exact assertions can fail.
Keep the expansion contract test aligned with the original source tests,
not only with a second copy of the migrated YAML's expected values.
Midscene 1.13.1 `test.maxConcurrency` limits projects, not cases. A single
project remains serial regardless of this setting. Do not claim case-level
parallelism without separate project shards and independently scoped registries.
Verify model vision with an image-only challenge; text-only preflight
responses and HTTP 200 do not prove the endpoint reads screenshots. Record the
actual response model version when diagnosing failures, because endpoint IDs
may be retargeted. Do not attribute base64 refusal messages to small UI elements
without a model-isolated control experiment.

For original contracts with intentionally nonvisual fixtures, use standard
recordToReport captures instead of inventing visual assertions. Extract their
recorder screenshot references as well as UI-context screenshots. When an exact
assertion has no agent trace, retain the failed-step HTML link and use the
nearest preceding capture from the same attempt for its preview.

When any platform produces no report, replace the archived site index with an
explicit incomplete-current-run page and links only to available current-run
reports. Never retain an older success redirect or invent a merged report,
screenshot, or pass for a platform that did not execute. Keep this behavior and
its regression tests synchronized with the native renderer before pushing Web.
